body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main, author's quick gate green on 689e0b91 (pins in `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_rapid.rs` and the `verify::stock_top` unit tests), body complete. Flagged ready; a gouge law, so it gets the high-tier review. Stacked on #1077: merge that first.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 689e0b91bfba1468d3d58aa04bf001c7641e645c -->
**Needs changes before merge** - one blocker: the new acquittal assumes a closed mesh and does not check it, so an open "from model" stock lets a rapid into real stock post.

Reviewed only this PR's own commits (`c6c658db..689e0b91`, i.e. on top of #1077), trial-merged with current `origin/main` (clean, nothing to merge). High-tier review: I read it adversarially, looking for rapids into stock that now pass.

### What I built, ran and tried
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-app --test stepped_stock_rapid` | 3 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test ladder_entry_height` | 4 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test operations` | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| `camcraft-app --test golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| `camcraft-sim --lib verify` (incl. the 7 `stock_top` tests) | 18 passed (filter `verify`) |
| `camcraft-sim` `posed_rapids` / `radial_rapids` / `sideways_rapids` / `vertical_rapids` | 5 / 15 / 3 / 16 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Throwaway probes (local only, reverted, never pushed) against `acquit_by_stock_top`, on a slab to Z 20 with a 4 mm tool diving to Z 22. These all stayed **convicted**, as they should:
- a boss whose corner pokes 0.35 mm into the rim at 45 deg (no facet vertex inside the disc);
- one triangle with all three vertices far outside and an edge 1 mm from the centre; a vertical wall facet whose plan crosses the disc; a huge high triangle containing the whole disc;
- a 0.02 mm thin rib under the rim (no sampling, so nothing slips between samples);
- an overhang: a plate Z 25..28 over the dive, held by a far pillar, with the dive ending under it (the plate's top facet is in the disc, so the whole column is judged, not only the end point);
- a tall boss under the holder only (10 mm off the centre: outside flute and shank, inside the holder's 16 mm);
- NaN in the dive's XY, and a NaN `z_tol`;
- a dive ending 0.01 mm into the slab.

`dist2_tri` is an exact plan distance (0 inside, either winding; degenerate plans read as their edges), and each facet lends its highest vertex. On a closed mesh the bound is sound.

### Requested before merge
1. **Open meshes fail open: a rapid into stock posts.** `crates/sim/src/verify/stock_top.rs:12-15` (module doc) proves the bound only "for a closed mesh", but nothing checks that. A "from model" stock is an imported mesh, and the importers do not enforce watertightness. Where the top facets over the dive are missing, `top_within` (`stock_top.rs:89-100`) only sees the facets *under* the material and acquits.
   Reproduction: in `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_rapid.rs`, make `casting()` drop the boss's two top facets (`boss.facets[4..12]` instead of `[2..12]`) and run the boss-over-the-hole case `[-12, 12, -12, 12]`:
   ```
   PR head:            Stock: dive #0 to Z 22; warns []; posted Ok(())
   acquit disabled:    Stock: dive #0 to Z 22; warns [RapidInStock { at: 0 }]; posted Err("post blocked - 1 warning(s): Op1: rapid move 0 travels below the clearance plane inside stock")
   ```
   The stock-sourced Bore posts a rapid to Z 22 into a boss that stands to Z 30. Main refuses it (the flat cap reads the walls' Z 30). The part-sourced Bore is still blocked here, but only by an unrelated stock-sim gouge verdict. Sim-level twin: the slab plus a boss shell without its top, dive at the boss centre to Z 22: `acquit_by_stock_top` returns `[]`.
   Fix: fail closed unless every solid is closed. For example, every undirected edge (exact endpoint match) is used by an even number of facets in its solid, checked next to `all_finite` (`stock_top.rs:51-55`). Then add a pinning test with an open boss shell that must stay convicted. The fixture in the PR's sim tests (two overlapping closed cubes) still passes such a check.

### Notes (not blocking)
- Tolerance: a band is acquitted at `tip + h >= top - z_tol` with `Z_TOL = 1e-6`, the same slack the column law uses. `model_excess` (#864/#911) is not read, but the column law does not read it for rapids either: a coarse dome whose real apex bulges above its highest mesh vertex is judged the same as before. Worth a line in the decision file.
- "Vertical" means XY drift `<= z_tol` (1e-6) and an upright or absent axis, so a lateral, diagonal or posed rapid cannot reach this path. Probed: a 3 mm drift stays convicted.
- Carried stock: `carried_stock::judged` replaces any non-box declared stock, and any box that does not hold the carried body, with the enclosing box. So the acquittal never reads a declared mesh lower than carried material. Fine.
- The modelled tool body (#835) is enclosed by `ToolGeom.holder_radius` (`BodyBands` refuses bands past the holder), and the holder is read as unbounded upward. Conservative.
- A move convicted by both the column law and the part solid law (`solid.rs`, same `RapidInStock` word) is cleared by one re-read. That re-read covers the part facets with the full stack, so it is sound on closed meshes. The open-mesh point above applies to it as well.
- Not exercised: the 3+2 site end to end (I read only that `stock_local` and `m_gen.facets` are both local and the path is local), and Thread's descent end to end.
- `generate.rs` grows by 5 net lines; the new files are 124 and 29 lines, with provenance lines. No process files touched.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Review blocker fixed on `6440858b` (plain push, still a draft): `acquit_by_stock_top` now reads a solid only if `stock_top_shell::closed_shell` proves it is one closed, outward shell (every undirected edge used by exactly two facets, once each way; non-empty, finite, no 3-D degenerate facet, one edge-connected shell, positive signed volume), else the conviction stands. Your open-boss case is pinned for both sources (`an_open_stock_mesh_proves_nothing_and_the_dive_stays_convicted`, which fails with the gate off), plus unit tests for open, non-manifold, duplicated, degenerate, inside-out, split, empty and non-finite solids. Quick gate green (16.1 min, 0 failed); clippy clean. The decision file says what the acquittal now relies on.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The open-mesh blocker from my first review is fixed, and no new blocker turned up.

This review covers the change since my first one (`689e0b91..6440858b`): the new `stock_top_shell.rs`, the gate in `stock_top.rs`, the new tests and the decision file. I trial-merged it with current `origin/main` (clean, nothing to merge).

|---|---|

### Attacks on the closed-shell gate (local throwaway probes, reverted, never pushed)
The first round's probes were rebuilt as **single closed shells**: two concatenated boxes now fail the gate, so the old probes would pass for the wrong reason. Each fixture was asserted to pass `closed_shell` before it was judged.
- **A boss corner poking 0.35 mm into the rim** (one closed box): convicted.
  - Positive control, a dive 2 mm over a box top: acquitted.
- **A tetrahedron** with all four vertices outside the disc and one plan edge 1 mm from the centre: convicted.
- **A 0.02 mm rib** under the rim: convicted.
- **An overhang**, built as a closed Γ-shaped extrusion: the arm at Z 25..28 stands over the dive, with air under it down to Z 22. Convicted.
- **An open boss patched with a back-to-back facet pair**, once far away and once sharing a vertex of the hole: `closed_shell` is false and the dive stays convicted. A hole's boundary edges are used once each. Only facets that use them in reverse close them, and those facets lie over the hole's plan, so they carry its height.
- **`-0.0` vs `0.0`**: read as one point. `to_bits` is otherwise injective, and NaN is refused before keying, so two different points can never collide into a false match.
- **Holder band and part solid**: the PR's own tests (`a_holder_band_over_the_boss_stands`, `the_part_reading_counts_too`) still pass. Every solid must pass the gate (`.all`).
- **Self-intersection**: the decision file's argument holds. `top_within` takes the **maximum over every facet whose plan meets the disc**; it does no parity or ray counting. Take any point that a closed surface encloses (non-zero winding, odd parity, or any definition between them). Its upward ray must cross that surface, at a facet whose plan covers the point and which stands above it. Folding or overlap cannot hide that facet.
- **Legitimate multi-shell solids** (a part with an inner void, several selected bodies, a casting plus a separate boss solid) fail the connectivity check. They keep main's conviction, which is conservative. No path acquits when the gate fails.
- **Same facet set**: the gate and the height read take the same slices (`solids`). At the 3+2 site those are `Frame::local_facets`, a pure per-vertex map: equal input bits give equal output bits, so closedness survives the mapping. If rounding ever merged two vertices, the result would read as degenerate or non-manifold, which refuses. There is no clipping or filtering between the gate and the read.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Cost.**
  - The gate is O(F): 213k facets in about 0.47 s per call, debug.
  - Each convicted dive then scans all facets once per band, 3 x F. That is about 0.5 s per dive on 213k facets in debug. A drill pattern of hundreds of holes on a fine casting could add minutes in debug, seconds in release.
  - A plan-space bucket index (or a per-op pre-filter by the bands' XY extent) would bound that if it ever shows up. It does not affect correctness.
- The decision file now names `model_excess` and self-intersection explicitly. Good.
- `stock_top_shell.rs` is 108 lines and `stock_top.rs` 123, both with provenance lines. No unwrap, expect or panic outside tests. NaN is refused before keying and in the volume and area checks.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
